Travancore was a Hindu kingdom at the southern tip of India, in what is now southern Kerala, from about 1729 to 1949. Marthanda Varma built it by conquering the small chiefdoms around him. In 1741 his army beat a Dutch force at the battle of Colachel, a rare defeat of a European power in India. In 1750 he gave his kingdom to the god Padmanabha of the Padmanabhaswamy Temple and ruled as the god's servant.

The kingdom grew rich on pepper, which the crown sold as a monopoly. The capital moved to Thiruvananthapuram in 1795. In 1789 Tipu Sultan of Mysore attacked its northern defence lines, which drew the East India Company into war against him. Travancore then became a Company ally and, after a failed revolt in 1809, a princely state under British control, like its neighbour Cochin.

In the 1900s it was known for its schools and high literacy. It joined India in 1949.
